pageInfo.subtitle: Master effortless multi-string economy of motion, finger-rolling mechanics, 3-, 4-, and 5-string arpeggios, and virtuosic speed.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Sweep picking is the ultimate technique for executing lightning-fast, multi-octave arpeggio cascades with crystalline clarity. Rather than picking each string with alternating strokes, your pick glides smoothly across adjacent strings in a single continuous brush stroke—downwards or upwards—while your fretting hand lifts each finger the microsecond after it is played. Championed by Frank Gambale, Yngwie Malmsteen, Jason Becker, and John Petrucci, true sweep picking mastery demands absolute synchronization between pick push and fretting-hand finger rolling.

items.text: The Continuous Brush Stroke: Move your pick in one unbroken falling or rising line across strings like a paintbrush—never treat a sweep as separate pick strokes.
Directional Pick Angle: Tilt the pick 15–30 degrees in the direction of the sweep (downward slant for down-sweeps, upward slant for up-sweeps) so the blade slices across strings.
The Barre-Free Finger Roll: When playing consecutive notes on the same fret across adjacent strings, roll a single finger pad smoothly from string to string without barring flat.
Acoustic Note Separation: Lift each fretting finger immediately after striking; notes must never bleed into one another like a strummed chord.
The High-E Turnaround: The highest note of the sweep on string 1 is struck with a downstroke and immediately followed by a pull-off to reverse pick direction smoothly.
Triad Sweeps (3-String Foundation): Master compact 3-string major and minor triad shapes on strings 1, 2, and 3 before attempting wide 5-string sweeps.
5-String Sweep Architecture: Connect low-string roots to high-string 3rds using the classic 5-string CAGED minor and major shapes.
7th Chord Sweep Extensions: Incorporate major 7th, minor 7th, and dominant 7th arpeggios with 2-note-per-string legato extensions.
Two-Hand Sympathetic Muting: Rest your right-hand palm heel across lower strings while using fretting index finger flesh to mute unplayed higher strings.
Metronome Subdivisions: Sweeping sounds messy when players rush ahead of the beat; practice with strict 16th-note or sextuplet metronome clicks.

exercises.title: 3-String Minor & Major Swept Triads
exercises.description: Start with compact 3-string triads on strings 3, 2, and 1. Push your pick through strings 3, 2, and 1 in a single downward motion, strike the high note on string 1, and pull off before sweeping upward back to string 3 across Am, G, F, and E triads.

patternNote.text: Stroke Path: Down-Down-Down ➔ Up-stroke on high note with pull-off ➔ Up-Up return stroke

notation.title: 3-String Swept Triad Sequences Across Am - G - F - E
notation.staveTitle: Fluid 3-String Swept Triads with High-E Turnarounds

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Do not strum the notes together like a chord. Lift each fretting finger the instant the pick leaves the string so each pitch speaks with pristine separation.

exercises.title: The Barre-Free Finger Roll (Consecutive Frets)
exercises.description: The finger roll is the biggest technical hurdle in sweep picking. When notes sit on the same fret across adjacent strings, you must roll the finger joint from string to string rather than barring flat. This exercise isolates the roll on fret 7, fret 5, and fret 9.

patternNote.text: Finger Rolling: Roll the pad of your ring finger across strings 3, 2, and 1 on fret 7 without barring flat

notation.title: Finger-Rolling Mechanics on Consecutive Frets
notation.staveTitle: Isolating Clean Finger-Roll Muting Across Adjacent Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Start on the tip of your finger on string 3, collapse to the middle pad on string 2, and roll to the flat pad on string 1. Every note must be completely muted as soon as the next is played.

exercises.title: Descending 3-String Sweep with Hammer Turnaround
exercises.description: Turnaround mechanics require precise timing: down-sweeping through three strings, striking the turnaround note, pulling off, and up-sweeping in reverse. Practice this continuous cycling motion across Am, Dm, and E7 shapes.

patternNote.text: Turnaround Loop: Down-sweep (3 notes) ➔ High pick ➔ Pull-off ➔ Up-sweep return (3 notes)

notation.title: Continuous 3-String Sweep Turnaround Loops
notation.staveTitle: Synchronizing Turnaround Pull-Offs and Reversing Sweep Strokes

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Do not pause at the turnaround. The change of direction should feel like a bouncing tennis ball—elastic, effortless, and rhythmic.

exercises.title: 4-String Minor 7th Sweep Arpeggio
exercises.description: Adding the 4th string expands your sweeps into sophisticated jazz-fusion and progressive metal territory. This exercise sweeps through 4-string Dm7, Em7, and Am7 arpeggios, incorporating the root, flat 3rd, 5th, and flat 7th.

patternNote.text: 4-String Sequence: Strings 4 ➔ 3 ➔ 2 ➔ 1 ➔ Turnaround on string 1 ➔ Ascend in reverse

notation.title: 4-String Minor 7th Sweep Arpeggios
notation.staveTitle: Traversing 4-String Minor 7th Arpeggios Across Shifting Positions

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Keep your picking hand's edge resting lightly on the lower unplayed strings to mute sympathetic vibrations as your sweep travels across the strings.

exercises.title: The Classic 5-String Yngwie Minor Sweep
exercises.description: This is the legendary 5-string sweep arpeggio pioneered by Yngwie Malmsteen and Jason Becker. Starting on the low A string (fret 12), sweep downward through five strings, hammer up to high A (fret 17), pull off, and sweep all the way back up to the 5th string.

notation.title: Classic 5-String Neoclassical Sweep Arpeggio
notation.staveTitle: High-Speed 5-String Minor Arpeggios Spanning Over Two Octaves

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice the 2-string roll on fret 14 (strings 4 and 3). Roll your ring finger smoothly without flattening out into a barre so notes don't ring simultaneously.

exercises.title: Symmetrical Diminished 7th Sweep Cascade
exercises.description: Diminished 7th arpeggios are completely symmetrical—every interval is a minor third (3 frets). This means you can shift the exact same sweep picking shape up by 3 frets repeatedly to create blistering neoclassical tension that resolves directly into the tonic.

patternNote.text: Symmetry Shift: Same diminished shape shifts up 3 frets: Fret 6 ➔ Fret 9 ➔ Fret 12

notation.title: Symmetrical Diminished 7th Sweep Shifts
notation.staveTitle: Minor-Third Symmetrical Sweeps Cascading Across the Fretboard

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how each 3-fret shift retains identical finger geometry. Diminished sweeps are the signature sound of Yngwie Malmsteen, Jason Becker, and Marty Friedman.

exercises.title: The Master Sweep Picking Etude: Neoclassical Velocity
exercises.description: This culminating 4-measure etude synthesizes all sweep picking principles: 5-string multi-octave sweeps over Am, 4-string cascades over Dm, shifting diminished tension over E7, and a soaring high-register resolution. Perform with laser timing and crystal-clear separation.

patternNote.text: Complete Sweep Synthesis: 5-String Sweeps + 4-String Arpeggios + Symmetrical Diminished Runs

notation.title: Master Neoclassical Sweep Virtuoso Etude
notation.staveTitle: Comprehensive 4-Bar Neoclassical Virtuoso Etude Across Am - Dm - E7

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Record your practice runs cleanly with a metronome. If you hear notes clumping together or buzzing, drop the tempo by 10 BPM and focus on relaxing your picking hand.

tips.title: Sweep Mastery Insights, Pitfalls & Daily Workout

items.title: 3 Mistakes That Kill Sweep Picking
items: The Strumming Trap: Leaving your fretting fingers down turns your arpeggio into a ringing chord strum. You must release each finger immediately after its note sounds.
The Stutter Pick: Picking each string with separate micro-strokes instead of one continuous falling or rising brush motion destroys sweep economy and caps your speed.
Flat-Barring consecutive frets: Flattening a finger across three strings produces muddy ringing. You must roll the finger joint so only one string is pressed at any millisecond.

items.title: Masters of Sweep Picking
items: Frank Gambale: The undisputed father of economy and sweep picking; revolutionized modern fusion by developing complete scalewise and arpeggiated sweep systems.
Yngwie Malmsteen: Popularized the 5-string and 3-string diminished sweep arpeggio in the rock world, executing blistering cascades with neoclassical swagger.
Jason Becker: Neoclassical prodigy who wrote some of the most intricate, multi-octave sweep arpeggios in guitar history on 'Perpetual Burn' and Cacophony albums.
John Petrucci: Dream Theater virtuoso known for surgical 5-string and 6-string sweeps integrated seamlessly into complex progressive metal time signatures.

items.title: The 15-Minute Daily Sweep Workout
items: Block 1: 3-String Finger-Roll Isolation (5 min) - Practice clean rolling on fret 7 across strings 3, 2, and 1 at 70 BPM, verifying zero note bleed.
Block 2: 5-String Yngwie Shape (5 min) - Cycle the 5-string A minor sweep pattern slowly, focusing on clean pick push and turnaround pull-off sync.
Block 3: Diminished Symmetrical Shifts (5 min) - Practice 3-fret symmetrical diminished shifts at 85 BPM, maintaining relaxed wrist oscillation.
